text:
B: Hiii! Oh, I love your kitchen, it's so tidy! I said that in the photo bit actually. I'm Chiamaka, I'm in Leeds.
A: Ha, thank you. It isn't always. Gemma, Hornchurch. Are you NHS? I saw the lanyard.
B: Yes! Acute medicine, speciality doctor at one of the big teaching hospitals. I've just come off four nights, so if I start talking nonsense, you know why. I'm knackered.
A: Four nights, God. I was NHS for about ten years, community paediatrics. Speech and language therapy. I'm private now.
B: Oh, private, very nice! Do you miss it?
A: No. Honestly, no. The caseloads were ridiculous and nobody listened to you. I went part-time after my second and, well, private made more sense. I set my own rates, I run my own waiting list, I'm not begging a manager for a room.
B: Waiting list, oh, tell me about it. Our ward is basically one long waiting list with beds in it. Sometimes it's me holding the whole place together on a night, you know, the only medic who knows where everything is.
A: Sorry, are you on your own overnight, then?
B: Well, sorry, sorry, not on my own, there's a registrar and the team. But you know what I mean, everyone comes to you.
A: Yeah, I do know. Are you going for consultant?
B: That's the plan! Within five years, by God's grace. I just need to finish my MRCP Part 2. Which I keep saying. Every year I say it.
A: You need to block the time out. Honestly. Put it in a calendar and treat it like a shift.
B: Look at you, you sound like my mum! She's a headmistress. But you're right. My paperwork is a disaster, my discharge summaries, oh my days.
A: I'm the opposite, I reread my reports about five times before I send them. It's not a good thing either.
B: No, that's a good thing! Do you have holidays planned? I need a holiday after these nights.
A: We do a villa every summer, Spain or Portugal. We did Lisbon for my fortieth, just me and Dean, no kids. Still the best trip I've had.
B: Lisbon! I went last year with my girls! Oh, the pastéis de nata, I ate about twelve. And we did that rooftop bar in Bairro Alto, I got such good photos.
A: We went to the tile museum, actually. And the Gulbenkian. It was more of a gallery trip for us.
B: Tile museum, okay, very cultured! I'm not a gallery person, I'll be honest. I'll go for the café.
A: At least you're honest. What do you do to unwind, then?
B: Choir at church, I'm an alto, and Love Island. Don't judge me!
A: I wasn't going to judge you. Well, a little bit.
B: Ha! Everyone says that, then they're watching it with me by week two!
A: I've got a book group. We're doing a Booker longlist one this month and I'm the only one who's finished it, as usual.
B: See, you are the organised one. I knew it from your picture.
